name: Acyclovir
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 800 mg orally every 4 hours, 5 times daily, for 7 to 10 days
200 mg every 4 hours, 5 times daily, for 10 days
400 mg twice daily for up to 12 months, then re-evaluate
10 mg/kg every 8 hours for 10 days, infused over 1 hour
Obese patients: dose by ideal body weight; never exceed 20 mg/kg every 8 hours; no bolus, intramuscular or subcutaneous injection

key_interactions.effect: Raised acyclovir half-life and AUC and lowered urinary excretion and renal clearance (studied with IV acyclovir).
key_interactions.action: The label states the effect without a dose rule; account for it when kidney function is reduced.

common: Nausea and/or vomiting (2.7%, short-course genital herpes)
IV: injection-site inflammation or phlebitis (about 9%), transient rise in serum creatinine or BUN (5% to 10%, more with rapid infusion), nausea or vomiting (about 7%)
serious: Renal failure, in some cases fatal
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura/hemolytic uremic syndrome (TTP/HUS) in immunocompromised patients
Neurologic reactions (confusion, hallucinations, seizure, encephalopathy; postmarketing)

contraindications: Clinically significant hypersensitivity (e.g., anaphylaxis, severe cutaneous adverse reactions) to acyclovir, valacyclovir or any component of the formulation
monitoring: Kidney function (dose by creatinine clearance; renal failure reported)
Neurologic status in older adults and in kidney impairment

pk.half_life_eskd: About 19.5 hours in anuria (IV label Table 2); about 5 hours during hemodialysis
pk.vd: About 1 L/kg (Vdss in children, IV label Table 3)
pk.dialyzability: Yes: half-life about 5 hours during hemodialysis; a 6-hour session lowers plasma levels by about 60%. PD: no supplemental dose after interval adjustment (label).

ESKD half-life now comes from the acyclovir IV label (19.5 hours in anuria); the VALTREX source was dropped.
Vd is a pediatric value (no adult Vd in either label); blank it if you prefer adult-only numbers.
Neurologic reactions are listed under postmarketing experience; the monitoring line is a clinical inference from the geriatric/renal text. Confirm or delete.
